chapters.s: Channa Grove turns the village’s world of bhut, pret, rakshas, loth and Budhba into a court of memory. Kabaddi becomes a way for untimely dead and incomplete names to enter collective testimony, while Ba’s handling of the gamchha links the ghostly game to the bridge-site water-burial that the living must investigate.

chapters.t: The Village on the Right Bank
chapters.s: Ba held up the torn corner of the gamchha. The smoke of dawn had not yet spread across the whole sky. The moment the date was stamped, the paper trembled faintly. The vibration reached Nand's hand. He felt as though Budhba the Ghost were speaking in Channa Grove: “Take care. A date can be the enemy of a name, and it can also be the boat that carries a name.…

Nand's application lay open on a table in the project office the next morning. The violet circle of the government stamp at the corner of the sheet still shone as though wet, as if the ink had not yet dried, as if some river inside it were still carrying a little current. After that the page seemed to fill itself. Nand went on writing. Outside, the river went on flowing. Inside Channa Grove, kabaddi continued. And all night the coconut leaves of Garh Narikel trembled as though each leaf had become a testimony ready to fly to…

Saryu's name was in the third line. Nand kept looking at it. That night kabaddi began again in Channa Grove. This time, as the ghosts crossed the boundary, they spoke one word: 'Court.' The prets answered: 'Date.' The rakshasas kept casting light. The loth did not laugh.…

When Nand Aruni reached the veranda of the district court with Devkinandan Chaube, he felt that he had entered not a building but an old pond. Dust lay upon the walls like moss. The coconut leaves of Garh Narikel moved late into that night. There was no wind. The leaves spoke by themselves—date, date, date—and between each date a name shone, written not on paper but on water, as though water itself were the final…

That day snow was falling outside Harvard's auditorium. Inside there was warm light, polished wooden chairs, gleaming screens, and identification cards hanging from every neck. From beneath the water came the answer: "So am I."
chapters.tu: the bright cadence of a Vidyapati song

chapters.s: When the market began to set the price of breath, the ghosts of Garh Narikel stopped their games for the first time and began watching the living—with the concentration of an old physician holding a finger to a pulse, except that the pulse was not his own but the pulse of the whole world.… At that very moment, far away in Garh Narikel, Panidubbi lifted the empty vial sunk in the water and kissed it, and from within the vial one drop fell—splash.

The ghosts in Channa Grove did not sleep for a long time that night. The list of untimely deaths had been made, yet a new worry sat upon Old Man Ghost's brow. The morning news said, "New opportunities in the online gaming industry." At the same time, a chapter title opened in Gop Kumar's file: "The Crocodile of the Screen." He knew that the next form of water-burial had begun.…

That night the kabaddi stopped in Channa Grove. It was an extraordinary thing. After that night the criminal web in Gop’s file stood clear—the bridge workers, the breath of the pandemic, gambling on the screen, the market in bodies. They were not separate. They were circles drawn on water. At the centre stood the human being.…
chapters.g: Budhba Ghost said, “Then change the name of guilt in this chapter. The body is not guilty. The market is. Hunger is not guilty. The one who sells hunger is. Shame is not guilty. The one who turns shame into a rope is.”

chapters.s: That night the ghosts in Channa Grove were again playing kabaddi, but the boundary of the game had changed. Earlier the line was drawn on the earth; now the water-drowned woman drew it in the air with her wet hair. The chapter had not ended; only the next face of the crime was about to open. The stream of money would now turn toward weapons, drugs and terror financing. But on this night Meera had saved her name.…

That night, after Mrinalini Arya’s testimony had been recorded and the theft of her private life had become evidence of a crime, the kabaddi in Channa Grove did not stop. The game only slowed. That morning Gop Kumar wrote one sentence in his diary: “When crocodiles begin laying eggs in bank accounts, know that the time has come to cleanse not the river, but the reckoning.”
chapters.g: Soumya closed her notebook, her voice holding more resolve than fatigue. “In this chapter we did not catch the names of all the crimes. We caught their rhythm. Once we know the rhythm, we can find the names again.”
chapters.tu: a blend of transplanting song and boatman’s song

chapters.t: Coconut Leaf on the Dark Web
chapters.s: When dawn spread over Garh Narikel, Channa Grove lay still with the fatigue of the night's game. The ghosts were seated once more upon their separate branches, but that day's stillness was not the silence of the dead. Far away, the black river kept flowing. But for the first time a coconut leaf floated upon it and did not sink.
